newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu goes on offensive over probe.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu goes on offensive over probe.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has come out fighting against opposition hopes his government could fall over a probe into alleged corruption.
Lawyer Yaakov Weinrot said on Sunday that Netanyahu had hired him to protect his interests in the investigation into January's short-lived appointment of an attorney general.
Weinrot confirmed an Israel Television report that at least part of Netanyahu's questioning by police last week was "under caution", triggering speculation the probe could topple him.
Under Israeli legal procedure, police caution people they question when they believe charges might be filed against them, said legal analyst Moshe Negbi.
Nissim Zvilli, secretary-general of the main opposition Labour party, said it was "beginning preparations for early elections" because the probe could bring down the government.
Later in Jordan at a news conference with King Hussein, Netanyahu cautioned Labour against preparing for his early political demise.

"I have one suggestion for them: Wait patiently. You have four good years in the opposition. I intend that you will enjoy another four years in the opposition after that...I'm going to continue to lead Israel in my way, to lead to peace, security, and economic prosperity," he said in answer to a question.
Police questioned Netanyahu for four hours last Tuesday about his appointment of Jerusalem lawyer Roni Bar-On, an activist in his Likud party, as attorney-general.

Israel Television said on January 22 that Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, on trial on corruption charges for the past three years and a key figure in the ruling coalition, had pressed to have Bar-On named to the post to arrange a plea bargain.
Bowing to such alleged pressure would fall under the criminal charge of breach of public trust, legal experts say.

According to the television report, Deri had demanded Bar-On get the attorney-general's job in exchange for Shas's support for Netanyahu's accord with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) on an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron last month.
Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid allegations by jurists and politicians that he was not qualified for the job.

Jordanian officials said Sunday's talks were overshadowed by Jordan's concerns over Israeli plans to build 6,500 new homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem. Netanyahu and the king glossed over the problem at their news conference.
Netanyahu has vowed to build the neighbourhood and has said he will put the plan before his ministers this week.

Israeli critics of the project say it will spark Palestinian rage that could prove more costly than gun battles in which 61 Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died last year after Netanyahu opened a tunnel entrance near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

According to interim peace deals, competing Palestinian and Israeli claims to Jerusalem are to be dealt with in "final status" peace talks slated to restart next month. Palestinians see the Israeli building plan as violating the status quo before talks.
